decision: Read the model card, config.json, and the fish-speech v3.0.0-beta reference code before designing anything
why: the whole engine depends on the exact layer types, shapes, and prompt format
result: architecture pinned: 40-layer Qwen3-Next style hybrid MoE backbone, 13-layer codebook tower, DAC codec at 44.1 kHz with 2048-sample frames

decision: Dropped MLX on the user's instruction; backbone and tower run on hand-written Metal compute kernels
why: user asked for own kernels on Apple silicon

decision: Codec (DAC encoder and decoder) goes through Core ML so it can use the Neural Engine; the 35B backbone stays on Metal
why: Apple exposes no kernel API for the ANE, Core ML is the only route, and a 35B MoE with a KV cache cannot live on the ANE anyway

decision: Weights are read in place from the Hugging Face cache via mmap; no converted copy on disk
why: the disk has 69 GB free and the weights are 41.5 GB

decision: Experts stay FP8 e4m3 with their 128x128 block scales and are dequantized inside the kernel through a 256-entry table
why: exact to the release, 3 MB per expert instead of 6 MB in bf16, and no conversion step

decision: Main-token logits are computed only for the 4097 candidate rows (eos plus the semantic band) instead of all 252288
why: the reference slices logits to those rows before sampling, so this is exact and saves 1 GB of reads per frame

decision: The faithfulness oracle is the fish-speech PyTorch code run on CPU with FP8 experts dequantized per selected expert; comparison is teacher-forced per step
why: the user asked for a faithfulness suite and a hill-climb; sampling diverges by design so only teacher-forced logits are comparable
